RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, August 13, 2012/Sravana 22, 1934 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Coal; Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution;
Corporate Affairs; Earth Sciences; Information and Broadcasting;
Law and Justice; Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; Mines;
Minority Affairs; New and Renewable Energy; Parliamentary
Affairs; Power; Science and Technology; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Exploration of coal reserves in SCCL
*41. SHRI PALV AI GOV ARDHAN
REDDY: Will the Minister of COAL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that, as per the
present estimates, the coal reserves in
Singareni Collieries Company Ltd. (SCCL)
would be exhausted in the next 25 years;
(b) whether it is also a fact that unless
SCCL goes in for 600 meters deep, it would
be difficult for it to survive;
(c) if so, what efforts the Ministry is
making to have a long-term perspective;
and
(d) what would be the estimated
expenditure involved to explore coal from
the depth of 600 meters?
Cable digitisation deadline
*42. SHRI A. ELA V ARASAN: Will the
Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s decision, to
extend its earlier cable digitisation deadline
from June 30 to October 31, is a set back
to DTH service providers as it would put a
strain on financial health of the industry;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has extended
the deadline in the interest of consumers;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Benefites to minorities from
Government  programmes
*43. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Prime Minister’s Office
(PMO) has asked the Ministry to ensure
that the five national minorities are being
benefited from Government programmes
and if so, how;
(b) whether an external agency is likely
to be hired to evaluate the Prime Minister’s
15 Point Programme for minorities;
(c) the disadvantages faced by Muslims
who hold about 5 per cent of Government
posts; and
(d) whether the Ministry has been asked
to streamline its programmes and root out
bottlenecks in schemes such as
scholarships?

16
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Shortage of power in remote rural
areas
†*44. SHRI PARVEZ HASHMI: Will
the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE
ENERGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is an
acute shortage of power in remote rural
areas of various States in the country;
(b) whether alternative energy through
solar panels is being provided to those
areas;
(c) the details of draft of the aforesaid
scheme and whether Government has any
other plan for expansion in this regard and
if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of results achieved
through this project in such areas?
Storage of foodgrains by FCI and
CWC
*45. SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAY AN
SINGH: Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Food
Corporation of India (FCI) and the Central
Warehousing Corporation (CWC) do not
have enough warehouses or the manpower
for safely stocking foodgrains and
protecting it from exposure to rodents and
other adversities;
(b) if so, the details of storage facilities/
manpower available with FCI and CWC
to store 250 million tonnes of wheat and
rice produced in the country this year;
(c) whether Government would
encourage private parties to build
warehouses in the country; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Changing of ownerships by coal
companies
*46. SHRI PRAKASH JA V ADEKAR:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of private companies
whom coal blocks were allocated during
2006-09 and who have changed/diluted, in
one form or the other, the ownership stakes
after allocation;
(b) the details of such coal blocks and
the details of the companies;
(c) the details of ownership changes and
the new companies to whom stakes were
transferred; and
(d) what action Government intends to
take in this regard?
Coal shortage at thermal power
stations
*47. SHRI T.M. SELV AGANAPA THI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that most of the
thermal power stations in the country are
battling with dwindling coal stocks and 28
stations are left with hardly seven days of
coal supplies;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that, due to
shortage of coal, all the power stations in
the country are not able to generate power
as per the need of the hour and even below
the targeted level; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
